questions.title: Railway Track Maintenance
questions.problem_statement: A railway network has stations connected as a tree. Each track has a maintenance cost. Answer route-cost queries and replace the cost of an existing track.
questions.input_format: First line: N R M, where M=N-1. Next M lines contain U V W. Next line contains Q. Each query is `1 A B 0` for a path-cost query or `2 U V W` to replace the cost of edge U-V with W.
questions.output_format: Print the sum of the answers of all type-1 queries.
constraints: The N-1 edges form a connected tree.
Every type-2 update refers to an existing edge.
The final answer fits in signed 64-bit integer.

solution.code: The three path answers are 5, 14 and 2; their sum is 21.

questions.title: Smart City Traffic Toll
questions.problem_statement:
A system contains an infinite binary tree of numbered nodes. Node i is directly connected to 2i and 2i+1.
        All edge costs initially equal zero. In this smart city traffic toll problem, operation type 1 adds t to every edge on the
        unique path from x to y. Operation type 2 asks for the current sum of edge costs on the path from x to y.
        Print the sum of all type-2 answers.
questions.input_format: First line: q. Each of the next q lines contains `1 x y t` for an update or `2 x y 0` for a query.
questions.output_format: Print one integer: the sum of all type-2 query results.
constraints: The total answer fits in signed 64-bit integer.

questions.title: Forest Ranger Safe Leaves
questions.problem_statement:
In forest ranger safe leaves, locations are represented by a tree rooted at node 1. Every node is either safe (0)
        or hazardous (1). A worker may reach a non-root leaf only if the path from node 1 to that leaf never contains
        more than M consecutive hazardous nodes. Count all reachable leaves.
questions.input_format: First line: N. Second line: M. Third line: K=N-1. Fourth line contains N binary values for nodes 1..N. Next K lines contain U V.
questions.output_format: Print the number of reachable non-root leaves.
constraints: The edges form a connected tree.
The root node 1 is never counted as a leaf.

solution.code: Leaves 4, 5, 6 and 7 exist. Paths to 4 and 5 have at most one consecutive hazardous node. Paths to 6 and 7 contain two consecutive hazardous nodes, so only 2 leaves are valid.

        more than M consecutive hazardous nodes. Count all reachable leaves.
questions.input_format: First line: N. Second line: M. Third line: K=N-1. Fourth line contains N binary values for nodes 1..N. Next K lines contain U V.
questions.output_format: Print the number of reachable non-root leaves.
constraints: The edges form a connected tree.
The root node 1 is never counted as a leaf.

solution.code: Leaves 4, 5, 6 and 7 exist. Paths to 4 and 5 have at most one consecutive hazardous node. Paths to 6 and 7 contain two consecutive hazardous nodes, so only 2 leaves are valid.
